svg.text: The core account: what supports what
An arrow A → B means A is used in the proof of B — directly, or through unlabelled lemmas. Assumptions on the left; each column is one step further from them.
Extracted from the Lean environment; arrows implied by longer paths are removed. A box with no incoming arrow rests only on definitions and unlabelled lemmas.

g.title: LeanDag.decided_mono — decisions are monotone in the view
LeanDag.View.mem_of_reaches — causal history does not escape a view
LeanDag.decided_none_of_leader_absent — an absent leader is skipped
LeanDag.exists_correct_mem_inter — two quorums share a correct validator
LeanDag.directCommit_of_leader_mem — a correct leader is committed
LeanDag.card_authorsAt_of_lt — the DAG is dense below its frontier
LeanDag.round_le_of_reaches — causal history is non-increasing in round
LeanDag.decided_full — decisions propagate to the full view
LeanDag.exists_correct_mem_creators_inter — two quorum-backed identifier sets share a correct author
LeanDag.certificates_eq_empty_of_directSkip — a skipped block has no certificate anywhere
LeanDag.exists_certificate_reaches_of_directCommit — a committed block's certificate is unavoidable from `r+3`
LeanDag.not_directCommit_of_directSkip — no block is both committed and skipped
LeanDag.indirect_agrees_with_direct — the indirect rule agrees with the direct
LeanDag.commits_recur_within — the committing slot, and its round
LeanDag.synchronisedOn_of_rate — the round of coverage, explicitly
LeanDag.eq_of_directCommit_of_creator_eq — at most one block per slot is directly committed
